newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's CANTV to slow new line installations.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's CANTV to slow new line installations.

text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV, 40 percent of which is to be sold in a global share issue in mid November, has decided to slow down the rate on new line installation due to lack of demand, the company said.
"Unsatisfied demand has gradually fallen in certain areas and cities to the point that in some places there is an over- saturation of lines," CANTV said.
CANTV said it had complied with the rate of line installations laid out in its concession contract drawn up when the company was partially privatized in 1991.

CANTV President Gustavo Roosen said recently that the company had boosted the number of lines per 100 inhabitants from 7.5 to 11.1 since a consortium led by GTE Corp bought a 40 percent stake in the company in 1991.
By the end of 1996 the country of 21 million inhabitants will have 3.164 million lines. The number of installed lines will rise to 3.752 million at the end of 2000 when CANTV's monopoly expires.
"To oblige CANTV to continue the rhythm of growth which was set in 1991 would force it to make large investments to offer services where there is no demand," Roosen said.

Investments will be focused on other telephone services such as the construction of telecommunication centers in low-income settlements where residents will have access to pay phones and fax and message services.
The Venezuelan economy is expected to record its third year of recession in the last four years in 1996.
CANTV said the pace of line installations could pick up again in 1998 when the results of an IMF-backed economic reform program begin to bear fruit.

CANTV added that it had decided to gradually eliminate cross subsidies which undercharge for local calls and overcharge for long distance and international calls by the year 2000 so that, "prices for all telephone services will be based on the cost of production."
